messages.content: Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

Recruitment: Amazon Mechanical Turk. Stable self-known background: age=23; gender=male; education=undergraduate; employment=student; ethnicity=White
Payment: 100 points earn USD1; fixed participation fee USD1.
Current game position: 1 of 8. Predicting the First-mover task. Display layout: First-mover task above Second-mover task. Current payoff table in points, (First, Second): first A, second A → (500, 500); first A, second B → (20, 800); first B, second A → (800, 20); first B, second B → (200, 200).
No earlier main-game responses.
What response did this person actually submit for the requested role-specific task?
B

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. The same anonymous pair plays the games in a randomized sequence, without feedback about the other person’s responses or outcomes between games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). The neutral labels A/B, rather than moral labels, are used in the experiment. The native display can put the First-mover task above or below the Second-mover task. Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. In each game each person answers two role-specific tasks: a First-mover task chooses neutral Option A or Option B, and a Second-mover task specifies one response, A or B, for each possible First-mover choice. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. The selected First-mover’s own First-mover choice and the selected Second-mover’s appropriate conditional response determine both payoffs. Only the selected game is paid; there is no accumulation of payoffs over eight games. The payoff table below lists (First-mover points, Second-mover points). Entry and revision order within a game is not recorded. The person’s other current-role response is not supplied as earlier information. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. The two conditional responses are one complete joint strategy. They are hypothetical contingencies, not observations of an actual First-mover choice. At the end, one game is randomly selected for the pair and the two roles are randomly assigned. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the complete Second-mover strategy. Output a JSON object with fields if_first_A and if_first_B; each must be A or B. Both branches belong to one response.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.

Predict one actual response in an online experiment with eight two-person games. All their completed previous games, including their own First-mover choice and complete Second-mover strategy, are provided in chronological order. No current or prior opponent choices are revealed before this decision. Background fields below were measured in the later questionnaire and are used only when reasonably stable and self-known before choice; absent or refused fields are not invented. Politics, survey-experience responses and fitted preference parameters are not used as prior traits. Predict only the First-mover response. Output exactly A or B.
